report.source_text: A PRBC transfusion was administered as the initial treatment, following which oral prednisone was administered at a dose of 2 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks and then tapered slowly. The patient was continued on maintenance oral prednisone at a dose of 0.3 mg/kg on alternate days and has since been observed to sustain a hemoglobin level of >9.0 g/dL without receiving further transfusions. As an operative repair of the CDH was not performed at the time, a follow-up of the condition was planned on outpatient basis.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 19-month-old male presented with recurrent macrocytic anemia, history of hydrops fetalis, and multiple congenital anomalies. Initial lab work showed severe anemia (Hb 5.4 g/dL), macrocytosis (MCV 105.9 fL), severely decreased reticulocyte count (0.9%), and elevated hemoglobin F (12.1%). Bone marrow study revealed normocellularity with marked erythroid hypoplasia (M:E ratio 18:1). Genetic analysis confirmed a heterozygous RPS19 gene mutation (c.380G>A, p.Gly127Glu), leading to a diagnosis of Diamond-Blackfan Anemia. Treatment with PRBC transfusion and oral prednisone resulted in sustained hemoglobin levels >9.0 g/dL without further transfusions.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with recurrent macrocytic anemia, history of hydrops fetalis, and multiple congenital anomalies including inguinal hernia, congenital cataract, strabismus, and delayed developmental milestones.
Initial hemoglobin was severely decreased (5.4 g/dL), with elevated mean corpuscular volume (105.9 fL) and severely decreased reticulocyte count (0.9%).
Bone marrow study showed normocellular structure with a very high myeloid-to-erythroid ratio (18:1) and markedly decreased erythropoietic cells, while other cell lines were unaffected.
Genetic analysis revealed a heterozygous RPS19 gene mutation, c.380G>A (p.Gly127Glu), confirming the diagnosis of DBA.
Treatment with PRBC transfusion and oral prednisone led to sustained hemoglobin levels >9.0 g/dL without further transfusions.
